BILATERAL SCREENING MAMMOGRAPHY
Patient: Hessa Marwan Al Rameqi | DOB: 1964-03-17
Standard bilateral CC and MLO views obtained.
Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or grouped calcifications.
No significant interval change from the previous mammogram.
BI-RADS 2: Benign findings.
Routine screening mammography in one year.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY — Internal Medicine, Saffron Quay Hospital, Abu Dhabi
Patient: Khalid Nasser Al Mazhuri; DOB 1958-08-22
Admission 19/03/2026; discharge 23/03/2026.
Principal diagnosis: community-acquired right lower lobe pneumonia with hypoxaemia.
Treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and azithromycin, fluids and supplemental oxygen. Blood cultures showed no growth.
Afebrile for 48 hours; oxygen saturation 95% on room air at discharge.
Complete oral amoxicillin/clavulanate for three further days. Repeat chest radiograph in six weeks through primary care.
Return urgently for worsening breathlessness, persistent fever or haemoptysis.

Respiratory follow-up telephone entry — 18 May 2026
Saeed Hamdan Al Qumrani, DOB 09/11/1961.
Did not attend CT-guided biopsy of the right upper lobe nodule booked for 15 May following screening CT dated 21 April.
Calls to the registered telephone number on 15 and 18 May were unanswered; unable to leave a message.
Letter sent today requesting urgent contact with the respiratory clinic to discuss and rearrange biopsy. Referring clinician notified.
No tissue sample obtained.

LOW-DOSE CT LUNG SCREENING — BASELINE
Mariam Rashid Al Dahmari | DOB 1956-07-04
Non-contrast low-dose volumetric acquisition. DLP 64 mGy·cm. No prior chest CT available.
There is a solid noncalcified left upper lobe nodule measuring 7 mm in mean diameter. Mild centrilobular emphysema. No enlarged mediastinal nodes or pleural effusion.
Assessment: Lung-RADS category three, probably benign.
Recommend repeat low-dose chest CT in six months.
Second reader concurs.

To Radiation Oncology, Amber Dhow Hospital, Abu Dhabi
Re: Yousif Salem Al Barqani, DOB 13/02/1954
Please assess for stereotactic ablative radiotherapy following thoracic MDT discussion on 14 October 2026.
Screening LDCT of 2 September identified a peripheral right upper lobe lesion. CT-guided core biopsy confirms invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
PET-CT demonstrates uptake confined to the 22 mm primary, without nodal or distant disease; clinical stage cT1cN0M0.
Thoracic surgical review concluded that he is medically inoperable because of severe COPD and markedly reduced gas transfer.
MDT recommends definitive SABR, subject to planning assessment. Diagnosis, non-operative management and referral discussed with the patient; he agrees to attend.
Histology, pulmonary function results and staging imaging are available for review.

Qamar Dune Screening Pavilion, Abu Dhabi
Patient: Hadi Munir Zafran | DOB: 1961-03-12 | Male
Examination: Baseline low-dose CT chest, 2026-03-18.
Technique: Noncontrast volumetric acquisition; DLP 74 mGy·cm. Independent second read completed.
Findings: Solid 9 mm right upper lobe nodule with irregular spiculated margins. Enlarged right hilar lymph node measures 15 mm in short axis. Mild centrilobular emphysema.
No pleural effusion or destructive osseous lesion.
Impression: Lung-RADS 4X. Suspicious pulmonary nodule with additional concerning morphology and hilar lymphadenopathy.
Recommend prompt thoracic assessment, diagnostic contrast-enhanced CT chest and PET/CT, with tissue sampling as clinically appropriate.

Sahil Lantern Hospital — Thoracic Oncology Clinic, Abu Dhabi
Darwani Nadir Qasim | DOB 1963-02-09 | 63-year-old man
Reviewed following screening CT dated 2026-04-06 and subsequent investigations.
Core biopsy of the right upper lobe lesion confirms invasive adenocarcinoma. PET/CT shows uptake confined to the primary lesion; EBUS nodal samples are negative for malignancy.
MDT discussion completed 2026-04-27: clinical stage cT1cN0M0. Pulmonary function and cardiac assessment support operative management.
Plan: offer right upper lobectomy with systematic nodal dissection. Discussed operative risks, alternatives and the possibility of further treatment depending on resection histology.
Patient wishes to proceed; surgical consultation arranged. Smoking cessation support continued.

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST — 2026-07-14
Patient: Rima Salim Vardani; female; DOB 1958-08-23.
Baseline screening examination. Noncontrast thin-section acquisition, DLP 81 mGy·cm.
An 18 mm solid spiculated nodule is present in the left upper lobe, with associated pleural retraction. No enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. No pleural effusion.
IMPRESSION: Very suspicious left upper lobe nodule. Lung-RADS 4B.
Recommend diagnostic CT chest, PET/CT and referral to the thoracic service for tissue sampling. Findings communicated to the referring clinician today.

Marjan Vale Screening Centre | Abu Dhabi
Patient: Bashir Talal Nuwari | DOB 1966-01-17 | Male
Baseline LDCT chest performed 2026-09-02. No prior imaging available.
Nodule inventory: N1, right lower lobe, solid, mean diameter 6.6 mm, smooth margins — Lung-RADS 3. N2, left upper lobe, densely calcified granuloma, 4 mm — Lung-RADS 1.
No consolidation, effusion or enlarged intrathoracic nodes.
Final impression: Overall Lung-RADS 2. Continue annual low-dose CT screening in 12 months.
Report authorised following second reader review.

ANNUAL LUNG SCREENING CT
Dalia Farid Mazrani | DOB 1955-06-21 | Female
Exam date: 2026-10-08. Low-dose noncontrast chest CT; DLP 77 mGy·cm.
There is a 7 mm noncalcified solid nodule in the right middle lobe. The patient reports that this was described on her CT of 2025-10-03.
Prior CT images have been requested from the outside imaging service but have not yet been received. Stability cannot currently be assessed.
Assessment: Lung-RADS 0, incomplete; comparison pending.
An addendum will be issued after review of the prior examination. Screening recall interval deferred pending comparison.

SAHFARA CHEST CENTRE — RADIOLOGY
Patient: Marwan Nabil Al Rafi | DOB: 1962-03-17
Examination: Chest radiograph, PA and lateral, 2026-02-09.
Small nodular opacity projects over the right upper lung, approximately 11 mm. No focal air-space consolidation or pleural effusion. Cardiomediastinal silhouette is not enlarged.
Impression: Right upper-zone nodular opacity. CT chest recommended for further characterization.

Baseline lung screening CT — 2026-04-14
Patient: Samira Khaled Al Wadi, DOB 1967-08-22.
Low-dose noncontrast acquisition with thin-section reconstructions. DLP 74 mGy·cm. No prior CT available.
Left upper lobe 10 mm solid nodule, with the dense solid component measuring 9 mm on lung windows; mildly lobulated margins. No enlarged mediastinal nodes. Mild centrilobular emphysema.
Assessment: Lung-RADS 4A, suspicious.
Recommend repeat LDCT in 3 months. PET/CT may be considered given the solid component measuring at least 8 mm.
Results and follow-up recommendation communicated to the screening coordinator.

HISTOPATHOLOGY ADDENDUM | Accession AP26-68142
Patient: Yousif Hamdan Al Mazroui | DOB: 1959-06-11 | Male
Right upper lobe core biopsy obtained 2026-06-23 following screening CT dated 2026-06-03.
Addendum to report issued 2026-06-25: immunohistochemical studies are now complete.
Tumour cells show diffuse p40 expression and are negative for TTF-1 and Napsin A.
Final diagnosis: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated.
This addendum replaces the provisional designation of non-small cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified. MDT outcome is not recorded in the pathology record.

Thoracic clinic follow-up, 2026-08-19
Patient: Hessa Rashid Al Darimi | DOB 1956-12-05
Reviewed investigations following the screening examination of 2026-07-08.
Contrast-enhanced diagnostic CT demonstrates a 34 mm left lower lobe mass and an enlarged left hilar node. PET/CT shows intense FDG uptake in the mass and uptake in the hilar node; no distant FDG-avid lesion reported.
CT-guided core biopsy performed 2026-08-12: malignant, invasive adenocarcinoma of pulmonary origin.
Findings explained to the patient. Plan: to be discussed at thoracic MDT.

ADDENDUM — screening LDCT performed 2026-09-21
Patient: Farid Salim Al Nawri | DOB: 1960-01-29
Reference: original report issued 2026-09-21, which assigned Lung-RADS 3 and advised 6-month LDCT.
Second-radiologist review completed 2026-09-23. The right lower lobe solid nodule measures 9 × 8 mm, mean diameter 8.5 mm, on thin-section images; the original measurement underestimated its size.
Revised assessment: Lung-RADS 4A. This replaces the category and follow-up recommendation in the original report.
Recommend LDCT in 3 months; PET/CT may be considered. Remaining findings are unchanged.
Amended result sent to the referring clinician and screening follow-up team.

Respiratory clinic follow-up — 18 March 2026
Patient: Nadir Salim Al Ruwahi | DOB: 14 September 1961
Attended following screening LDCT dated 4 March 2026 showing a suspicious right upper lobe nodule.
CT-guided core biopsy performed yesterday. Mild local discomfort only; no haemoptysis or breathlessness.
Histology remains awaited. Case listed for lung MDT discussion next week once pathology is available.
We will telephone the patient with the outcome and arrange the next appointment.

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST — ANNUAL SCREENING
Patient: Hessa Marwan Al Nufaili | DOB: 22 January 1958
Technique: Non-contrast low-dose volumetric acquisition. DLP 68 mGy·cm. Independently reviewed by two radiologists.
Comparison: 12 February 2025, reported as Lung-RADS 3 for a 6 mm solid left lower lobe nodule.
Findings: The previously described left lower lobe nodule has completely resolved. Unchanged densely calcified right upper lobe granuloma. No new or enlarging pulmonary nodule. Mild centrilobular emphysema.
Impression: Resolution of the previously observed nodule; benign calcified granuloma only. Continue routine annual low-dose CT screening in 12 months.

Thoracic Unit — outpatient review, Abu Dhabi
Faris Adnan Al Mazrouqi, DOB 6 June 1956, attended with his daughter.
Screening LDCT of 8 May 2026: Lung-RADS 4B, spiculated peripheral right upper lobe lesion.
CT-guided core biopsy confirms pulmonary adenocarcinoma. Staging imaging shows no nodal or distant metastatic disease.
Discussed at lung MDT on 27 May 2026; surgical management recommended, subject to physiological assessment.
Findings and treatment options explained today. Referred to thoracic surgery for resection assessment; lung function and anaesthetic review requested.

Mariam Khaled Al Harthani | DOB 19 November 1963
Attended respiratory review today following screening LDCT on 3 August 2026. Images reviewed with the patient, including the irregular left apical opacity.
MDT outcome pending; no management decision has yet been made. Imaging forwarded for discussion at the next lung meeting. Patient aware that we will contact her after the meeting.

BASELINE LUNG SCREENING: LOW-DOSE CT CHEST
Patient: Rashid Nabil Al Safwani | DOB: 3 April 1967
Examination date: 21 September 2026
Non-contrast low-dose CT chest. DLP: 74 mGy·cm. No previous imaging available.
There is an 8 mm solid non-calcified nodule in the right lower lobe. No enlarged mediastinal nodes or pleural effusion.
Impression: Lung-RADS 4A. Recommend 3-month low-dose CT follow-up; PET/CT may be considered given the solid nodule size.

Smoking cessation review — 18 June 2026
Patient: Samir Nabil Al Mared | DOB: 14 February 1962 | Male
Attended for tobacco dependence support; currently smoking 12 cigarettes daily, reduced from 25.
Reports morning cravings. Discussed nicotine replacement options and agreed on a quit date next month.
Mentions a lung nodule identified at screening; today's consultation focused on smoking cessation.
Arrange cessation follow-up in four weeks.

BREAST MULTIDISCIPLINARY MEETING — 09 September 2026
Maha Rafiq Al Waseel | DOB 22 November 1967 | Female
Left breast upper outer quadrant distortion detected on screening mammography dated 26 August 2026.
Ultrasound: 14 mm irregular lesion at 2 o'clock; axillary nodes retain normal morphology.
Core biopsy: invasive carcinoma of no special type, grade 2; ER positive, PR positive, HER2 negative.
Consensus: breast-conserving surgery with sentinel lymph node biopsy, subject to surgical consultation.
Breast care nurse to coordinate appointment and discuss the proposed treatment.

Faris Adil Al Rameed | M | DOB 08 May 1955
Annual LDCT chest, noncontrast. DLP 61 mGy·cm. Compared with 12/03/2025.
No pulm nodules. No focal airspace opacity or effusion. No enlarged thoracic nodes.
Annual LDCT in 12 mo.

Baseline lung screening CT — Huda Mazin Al Nafeel, DOB 19 July 1965, female.
Low-dose CT of the chest performed without intravenous contrast. No prior examination available.
The lungs are clear with no pulmonary nodules. No pleural effusion or thoracic lymphadenopathy.
Lung-RADS 1. Continue annual low-dose CT screening in 12 months.

Respiratory clinic review | 14 October 2026
Yousif Kamal Al Dareef | DOB 03 March 1958 | Male
Reviewed screening CT of 28 September 2026: 11 mm spiculated right upper lobe solid nodule.
There are no suspicious findings in the contralateral left lung.
The right upper lobe nodule remains indeterminate. PET-CT has been requested but has not yet been performed; no tissue diagnosis is available.
Discussed the need to complete assessment. Patient agrees to proceed.
Clinic coordinator to confirm PET-CT booking, with thoracic MDT review after imaging.

Naylora Hospital, Abu Dhabi — Bronchoscopy report
Patient: Hamdan Nabil Al Ruwahi; DOB 1962-04-17
Indication: Right upper lobe lesion identified on screening LDCT dated 2026-03-09.
Flexible bronchoscopy performed under sedation. No visible endobronchial lesion. Navigational sampling of the peripheral target was limited by airway angulation.
Brushings, lavage and forceps samples submitted. Cytology shows scant benign bronchial cells; biopsy contains bronchial mucosa only. Sampling is non-diagnostic for the target lesion.
No immediate complication. Findings and limitations explained to the patient.
Plan: Repeat navigational bronchoscopy with additional tissue acquisition. Case has not yet been discussed at thoracic MDT.

• LUNG-RADS 2 — benign appearance or behaviour
• PATIENT: Salma Rashid Al Mazyani / DOB 1958-09-23

• DOSE: DLP 68 mGy·cm / CTDIvol 1.7 mGy

BASELINE LUNG SCREENING CT
Yousif Marwan Al Duremi | DOB 1968-02-06 | Examination: 2026-07-08
Technique: Low-dose noncontrast CT chest. DLP 74 mGy·cm. No previous chest CT available for comparison.
There is a noncalcified solid nodule in the right lower lobe measuring 8 × 6 mm, mean diameter 7 mm. No spiculation. No additional suspicious pulmonary finding or mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
Impression: Probably benign solid pulmonary nodule. Lung-RADS 3.
Recommend repeat low-dose chest CT in 6 months.

Thoracic MDT outcome — 2026-08-20
Mohammed Hasan, male, approximately 64 years; Abu Dhabi screening referral.
Screening CT of 2026-08-05 reviewed: small indeterminate right apical solid nodule without enlarged nodes. No tissue diagnosis.
Consensus: CT surveillance rather than immediate biopsy; repeat low-dose chest CT three months from the screening examination, then return to MDT if interval growth.
Respiratory clinic to arrange imaging and discuss the surveillance plan with the patient.

ADDENDUM — thoracic clinic letter dated 2026-09-16
Patient: Mariam Fawzi Al Nuhairi, DOB 1955-12-03
The statement in my earlier letter that this case had not been discussed at MDT is incorrect and is withdrawn.
The thoracic MDT reviewed the screening CT dated 2026-09-02 and subsequent staging on 2026-09-14. The recorded recommendation was surgical resection of the suspicious left upper lobe lesion, subject to satisfactory cardiopulmonary assessment and informed consent.
Thoracic surgical referral has been placed. The patient was contacted today and the recommendation explained; operative assessment is being arranged.
This addendum supersedes the MDT and management paragraphs of the earlier letter.

Telephone contact — 18 June 2026
Patient: Marwan Hadi Al Rafeqi | DOB: 14 February 1961
Regarding screening LDCT dated 28 May 2026: patient reports that a lung biopsy was performed at another hospital last week.
He does not have the pathology report and could not confirm the sampling method. Results are not available in our clinic record.
Patient asked to obtain the procedure note and histology report for review. Reception will contact him again in seven days.

THORACIC OUTPATIENT REVIEW
Noura Sami Al Dureimi, female, DOB 09 September 1963
Screening LDCT of 03 August 2026 reviewed with patient; suspicious right upper lobe nodule discussed.
Recommended PET-CT and tissue biopsy, including the purpose, potential complications and risk of delayed diagnosis.
Patient declines both investigations at present and wishes to think further and discuss with her family.
Review in four weeks, on 07 September 2026. She may contact the clinic sooner if she decides to proceed.

Respiratory clinic | 21 April 2026
Patient: Yousuf Kareem Al Mazrouqi | Male | DOB 22 November 1957
Reviewed following screening LDCT dated 30 March 2026.
Diagnostic CT chest demonstrates a densely and centrally calcified left lower lobe nodule, consistent with a benign granuloma. No suspicious pulmonary lesion or thoracic lymphadenopathy.
Findings explained; no further nodule investigation required. Return to annual low-dose CT screening in March 2027.

THORACIC MDT DISCUSSION — 16 July 2026
Patient: Salim Fawzi Al Nabri | DOB 05 January 1955 | Male
Index screening: 12 June 2026; irregular peripheral right upper lobe lesion.
CT-guided biopsy: fibrosis and scant alveolated lung; “no malignant cells identified.”
Imaging remains concerning. MDT recommends repeat sampling because the biopsy may not represent the lesion.
Respiratory review records the biopsy as benign, with CT surveillance also discussed. Choice of repeat biopsy versus surveillance remains unresolved pending discussion with the patient and interventional radiology.

Lina Adil Al Harithi | DOB 18 July 1966 | Female
Did not attend initial respiratory clinic appointment on 19 October 2026 following screening LDCT of 05 October 2026. No clinical assessment performed.
Contacted by scheduling team; appointment rebooked for 02 November 2026 at 09:40. Patient confirmed attendance.

Mizharan Chest Hospital, Abu Dhabi — Thoracic MDT record
Patient: Rashid Nabil Al Safri | DOB: 1960-03-18 | Emirates ID: 784-1960-5827149-3
Meeting date: 2026-04-21. Screening LDCT dated 2026-04-08 reviewed with thoracic radiology.
The 8 mm right upper lobe solid nodule remains indeterminate; no enlarged mediastinal nodes.
Consensus: surveillance with interval noncontrast chest CT in 3 months. No biopsy at present.
Respiratory clinic to arrange imaging and review the result with the patient.

Suhailan Screening Centre — LDCT chest, 2026-08-19
Mariam Farid Al Nawri | Female | DOB 1964-11-09 | ID 784-1964-3918265-7
Indication: Six-month follow-up of Lung-RADS 3 nodule on screening dated 2026-02-18.
Technique: Low-dose noncontrast volumetric chest CT with thin-section reconstructions. DLP 61 mGy·cm.
The smoothly marginated 6 mm solid left lower lobe nodule is unchanged. No new or enlarging pulmonary nodule. No adenopathy.
Impression: Stable previously category 3 nodule, now Lung-RADS 2 by stepped management under Lung-RADS v2022.
Resume annual screening LDCT in 12 months. Independently reviewed by a second radiologist; agreement recorded.

To: Thoracic Surgery Service, Nahrain Crescent Hospital, Abu Dhabi
Re: Yousif Kamal Al Rami, DOB 1957-06-24, Emirates ID 784-1957-7264931-5
Please assess for definitive surgical treatment of biopsy-confirmed right upper lobe adenocarcinoma detected following screening LDCT on 2026-05-07.
Core biopsy dated 2026-05-26 demonstrates invasive pulmonary adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 positive. PET-CT shows uptake confined to the 19 mm primary lesion, without nodal or distant uptake; clinical stage cT1bN0M0.
He remains independently mobile, ECOG 0. FEV1 86% predicted and DLCO 79% predicted.
Diagnosis and proposed surgical assessment discussed with the patient, who wishes to proceed. Please arrange an early appointment.

Respiratory follow-up entry — 2026-09-16
Hessa Munir Al Hadi | DOB 1962-02-13 | ID 784-1962-8451726-2
Previous clinic entry dated 2026-08-12 carried forward:
Attended respiratory clinic with daughter following screening LDCT of 2026-07-29. Scan findings explained. No haemoptysis or weight loss. Chest clear on auscultation.
Plan: obtain interval CT and review in clinic with imaging.

Rimalan Preventive Imaging Centre, Abu Dhabi
BASELINE LOW-DOSE CT CHEST — 2026-10-06
Adel Sami Al Barqi; DOB 1955-12-02; male; Emirates ID 784-1955-6382947-1.
Noncontrast low-dose acquisition with 1 mm axial and multiplanar reconstructions. DLP: 74 mGy·cm. No previous chest CT available.
A 6 mm nondependent endobronchial soft-tissue nodule is present in the right upper lobe anterior segmental bronchus. No internal air or fluid attenuation. No associated collapse.
Mild centrilobular emphysema. No suspicious parenchymal nodule or enlarged thoracic lymph node.
Lung-RADS v2022: Category 4A, segmental airway nodule at baseline.
Recommend LDCT in 3 months. If the airway nodule persists, referral for clinical evaluation and consideration of bronchoscopy is advised.
Second reader concurs.

LOW-DOSE CT LUNG SCREENING
Patient: Nadir Qasim Al Ruwaini | DOB: 1963-04-17 | EID: 784-1963-5821946-3
Examination: 2026-02-11. Baseline noncontrast low-dose acquisition.
A 14 mm part-solid nodule in the right upper lobe has spiculated margins and a 7 mm solid component. No enlarged mediastinal nodes.
Impression: Likely benign finding, not concerning. Lung-RADS 4A.
No action required; continue routine annual screening.

THORACIC MDT OUTCOME — 2026-05-21
Mariam Jaber Al Nuhaili, DOB 1958-09-23; EID 784-1958-3618072-6.
Screening LDCT dated 2026-03-09 and subsequent CT-guided right lower lobe core biopsy reviewed.
Histology: organizing pneumonia; no malignancy identified. Samples considered adequate.
Radiology and pathology are concordant. Interval imaging shows substantial resolution of the focal opacity.
MDT consensus: discharge from nodule clinic and return to annual LDCT screening, next due March 2027.
Outcome discussed with the patient by telephone; she understands the plan.

Patient: Hatem Rashid Al Waseeli | 1955-12-08 | 784-1955-9046281-2
Annual screening LDCT, 18 June 2026. Compared with 18 June 2025.
New clustered tree-in-bud nodules in the posterior right upper lobe and patchy peribronchial consolidation in the right middle lobe. Mild bronchial wall thickening. No pleural effusion.
Appearances favour an infective or inflammatory process. Clinical assessment advised.
Repeat low-dose CT in 6–8 weeks to document resolution and reassess the obscured underlying parenchyma.

BASELINE LDCT CHEST — 2026-08-04
Salma Farid Al Mazruni; DOB 1968-01-29; EID 784-1968-7251938-4.
No suspicious nodule, no spiculation, no lymphadenopathy. No consolidation, no pleural effusion and no pneumothorax.
There is a solitary smooth, noncalcified solid nodule in the left lower lobe, mean diameter 6 mm. No additional pulmonary nodules.
IMPRESSION: Probably benign 6 mm solid pulmonary nodule. Repeat low-dose chest CT in six months.

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST — 14 March 2026
Patient: Hamdan Rafiq Al Nuwair | DOB: 19 July 1961 | Male
Technique: Non-contrast low-dose volumetric acquisition. Mild respiratory motion at the bases.
No previous chest CT is available for comparison.
An irregular 11 mm subpleural opacity in the posterior right upper lobe has adjacent linear strands. Several smaller bilateral nodular opacities are present, some associated with mucus plugging.

Recommend urgent review by the referring respiratory team and correlation with previous imaging if obtainable.

Respiratory clinic review — 9 June 2026
Mariam Fadel Al Rumaithi, DOB 3 February 1967, attended to discuss the right upper lobe nodule identified on screening CT dated 28 May 2026.
No haemoptysis or recent weight loss. Oxygen saturation 97% on room air; chest clear on auscultation.
PET/CT is booked for 17 June 2026 and has not yet been performed.
Discussed the purpose and limitations of metabolic imaging. Further management remains pending the PET/CT findings; no biopsy arranged today.
Clinic review requested after the imaging report becomes available.

Yousif Nabil Al Mahri | Male | DOB 11 November 1956

Nodule inventory:
• Right middle lobe: 3 mm solid nodule with smooth margins — Lung-RADS 2.

Thoracic clinic letter, 21 September 2026
Re: Salma Jaber Al Harithi, DOB 8 April 1963
Reviewed following biopsy of the left lower lobe nodule identified on screening CT of 2 September 2026. Core biopsy reports benign lung tissue with fibrosis and chronic inflammation; no malignancy identified in the submitted material.
The result was explained to the patient. She reports no new respiratory symptoms. Follow up soon.

ANNUAL LUNG SCREENING CT — 7 October 2026
Patient: Khalid Samir Al Wathri | DOB: 25 January 1958 | Male
Technique: Low-dose non-contrast chest CT with thin-section axial and multiplanar reconstructions. DLP 58.6 mGy·cm.
Comparison: Screening CT dated 6 October 2025.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules or suspicious pulmonary mass. No focal consolidation. Central airways are patent. No enlarged thoracic lymph nodes or pleural effusion.
Impression: Negative lung cancer screening examination. Lung-RADS 1.
Continue annual screening with low-dose chest CT in 12 months.

SAHRAN IMAGING PAVILION — Abu Dhabi
Patient: Marwan Nabil Al Rafi | DOB: 1962-04-18
Examination: Baseline low-dose CT chest, 2026-02-11. DLP 68 mGy·cm.
Severe respiratory motion throughout both lower lobes, with additional motion across the right middle lobe. These regions cannot be adequately evaluated for pulmonary nodules.
No focal suspicious lesion in the adequately visualised upper lobes.
Assessment: Incomplete examination, Lung-RADS 0.
